title: tyrus Project Configuration
description: Configuration schema for an tyrus project (tyrus.json).

description.description: A short description of the project.

target.description: The project template scaffolded by `tyrus new`. This is informational and reserved for target-aware tooling.

build.description: Optional build configuration. When omitted, optimization is disabled by default.

optimize.description: Whether to compile with optimizations by default.

development.description: Optional settings that apply only while the program runs with TYRUS_ENV=development.

https.description: When true and TYRUS_ENV=development, a server started without `tls` serves HTTPS with a `localhost` certificate signed by a local development certificate authority, created once in the user configuration directory. Ignored in every other environment.

runtime.description: Optional asynchronous runtime configuration, baked into the compiled program.

workerThreads.description: How many worker threads the asynchronous runtime may use. Defaults to the number of logical CPUs. The TYRUS_WORKER_THREADS environment variable overrides this value at startup.

database.description: Optional database connection and runtime configuration.

backend.description: Database engine used by this project.

path.description: SQLite database file path, relative to the project root.

connectionEnv.description: Environment variable containing the database connection string for MySQL, PostgreSQL, or MongoDB.

schema.description: Path to the generated database schema snapshot. Defaults to tyrus-db-schema.json.

pool.description: Optional connection pool limits and timeouts for server databases.

tls.description: Optional TLS certificate files for server database connections.

sqlite.description: Optional SQLite journal and synchronization settings.

scripts.description: Named scripts runnable through the tyrus CLI.

envFile.description: Path to the .env file, relative to the project root. When set, its variables are typed and validated, exposed through `process.env`, and a `.env.example` mirror is kept in sync.

envSealed.description: When true, build encrypts envFile to target/.env.sealed with the project seal key, and the binary loads only the sealed env file next to the executable.

imports.description: Static aliases that map import prefixes beginning with # to directories relative to the project root.
